messages:
jordan: Heads-up — nightly benchmark alerted a quality drop when serving the new int4 kernel on guanaco-6b. CI regression: 3.8% BLEU-equivalent drop on the summarization suite. https://dash.internal/redwood/bench/1776 :eyes:
pranav: ugh. is this the new kernel from #4321 (kernel-refactor) or the quant pipeline change?
elyse: looks tied to the quant encoder path. I saw mismatched softmax scaling in the trace earlier. low-level change landed in PR 4387.
sara: pinging perf-bot for the trace artifact + exact inputs used in the failure case. can someone paste the failing example?
perf-bot: nightly-run/177600: guanaco-6b | int4-kernel | dataset=rdw-summaries-v2 | unit=bleu | baseline=0.621 | candidate=0.597 | delta=-0.024 | artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/177600/trace.tar.gz
pranav: thanks. I pulled the trace. Quick sanity: the candidate used `quant_scale=0.98` vs baseline `1.0` in the runtime config. Could that explain the shift?
jordan: possible. but offline eval with `quant_scale=0.98` on cpu sims only lost ~0.5%. this is much bigger. suspect subtle KV-cache alignment or attention rounding when combined with the new fused matmul.
elyse: I can repro locally on a small subset. Running `./tools/bench --model=guanaco-6b --quant=int4 --profile --seed=42 --cases=100` now. Will share profiler timeline.
sara: tagging @pranav for a quick review of the kernel PR — if we revert the fused matmul commit, we can validate rollback impact quickly. PR: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/4387
pranav: I can review in ~20m. If the profiler shows divergence in attention scores, we should run the numeric diff harness: `python infra/numeric_diff.py --base=baseline.json --cand=candidate.json --topk=5` to get token-level deltas.
jordan: sharing one failing example (shortened):
```
INPUT: "Summarize: Redwood's inference thesis and platform differentiators..."
BASELINE_OUTPUT: "Redwood is a developer-first platform for running and optimizing LLM inference..."
CANDIDATE_OUTPUT: "Redwood is a platform for inference that focuses on cost and latency..."
```
sara: candidate looks like it dropped some context and defaulted to a shorter phrasing. not just word choice. :thinking_face:
elyse: profiler update: timeline attached -> shows additional stall in `kv_upsert` around step 11 and a spike in quant dequant ops when fused matmul path is active. Uploading flamegraph: s3://redwood-ci/fg/177600/fg.svg
pranav: can you also dump raw attention matrices for that example? I want to compare magnitudes. small script: `python tools/dump_attn.py --case 11 --out=attn_case11.npz`
elyse: done. pushed attn_case11.npz to the same artifacts bucket.
perf-bot: regression-alert-acknowledged by @jordan @elyse. Created issue runtime#912 with link to artifacts and nightly stats.
jordan: next steps proposal: 1) Elyse runs an A/B where we enable fused matmul but force baseline `quant_scale=1.0` to isolate scaling; 2) Pranav does code review for 4387 and flags any numeric casts; 3) Sara prepares canary plan to revert fused matmul if A/B fails.
pranav: I skimmed 4387 — suspicious cast in `fused_matmul.cpp` line ~214: `(float)__half2float(acc)` — might be truncating in the reduce path. I'll annotate PR with comments.
elyse: running the A/B now (two configs on same hw):
- cfgA: fused_matmul=on, quant_scale=0.98
- cfgB: fused_matmul=on, quant_scale=1.00
Expecting to isolate whether scale is the primary driver.
sara: also queued a quick canary job to Dedicated pool so we can smoke test latency impact after any change. job id: ded-canary-177600-1
jordan: timeline: please post results in this thread. if delta > 1.5% BLEU still, we'll schedule a 30m async triage. I can host the call. :calendar:
pranav: review comments posted. marking two spots for potential precision loss. will re-run unit numerics locally and report back in ~45m.
elyse: A/B results (100 cases each): cfgA delta vs baseline = -2.6%, cfgB delta vs baseline = -0.9%. so making quant_scale 1.0 helps but doesn't fully recover. attached per-case CSV s3://redwood-ci/csvs/177600/ab_results.csv
sara: interesting — that suggests both scaling and fused path interact. can we try fused_matmul=off + quant_scale=0.98 to see the other axis?
elyse: queued that run now.
jordan: thanks all. consensus leaning toward reverting fused matmul until we pinpoint numeric edge-cases. but let's hold action until we see the fused_off run. if fused_off recovers to <0.5% delta we can revert.
perf-bot: fused_off run complete: delta = -0.4% (100 cases). artifact: s3://redwood-ci/artifacts/177600/fused_off.tar.gz
pranav: that nails it — fused path introduces an interaction that amplifies quant rounding. I'll open a revert PR and include regression tests (numeric diffs and the failing case).
elyse: OK I'll help with a minimal repro and add an integration check to nightly that runs the 100-case harness on the quantified kernels.
sara: I'll prepare the canary revert plan and coordinate with oncall for a short rollback window tomorrow 09:30 PT.
jordan: perfect. can someone drop a link to the revert PR when ready and ping #eng-releases? do that as a separate thread but link back here. :thumbsup:
pranav: will do — expect PR within the hour.
elyse: posting heatmap and notes to the issue runtime#912. closing loop here for now.
jordan: thanks everyone — great async troubleshooting. follow-ups in issue runtime#912 and PR 4399."
